newsitem.title: UK: World drug sales up 7 pct in first quarter - IMS.
newsitem.headline: World drug sales up 7 pct in first quarter - IMS.

text.p: Pharmaceutical sales in ten of the world's leading markets rose by seven percent in the first three months of 1997 in local currency terms, market researcher IMS International said on Monday.
IMS said North America was the fastest-growing region, with sales in the U.S.and Canada rising by 11 percent.
Sales in Japan showed a strong recovery, rising by six percent after gains of just one percent in January and February.

Growth in Europe continued to lag at an overall three percent. France, where sales rose by five percent, widened its lead over Germany as the largest single market for pharmaceuticals in Europe, with sales in Germany dropping by three percent.

By category, IMS said the strongest growth was in central nervous system (CNS), anti-infective and sensory organ drugs, which all saw growth of 12 percent.
In North America the growth in anti-infective sales was 20 percent and in CNS treatments was 16 percent, IMS said.
